scenario: Size difference on a known cancer + a qualified negative that does not deny probably benign calcifications (SPU) + a missed second lesion (MIS)
description: Built from breast-mg/findings_{gt,pred}/example_3 (constructed diagnostic mammogram for extent of a known cancer). The index malignancy is matched despite its smaller pred size; two axillary negatives match; gt 'no suspicious mass, calcifications or architectural distortion' in the right breast is a qualified negative, so it does not deny the pred calcifications called probably benign: the pred calcifications stay unmatched (SPU) and so does the gt negative; the fine pleomorphic calcifications in another left quadrant, which the pred leaves out, are MIS.

user.indication: 52-year-old woman with biopsy-proven invasive ductal carcinoma of the left breast. Evaluate extent of disease before surgery.

pred_findings.text: Extremely dense breasts (ACR breast density d).

Biopsy-proven malignancy in the left breast at 1 o'clock, upper outer quadrant, 6 cm from the nipple, seen as a 1.9 x 1.8 cm irregular mass with spiculated margins containing the biopsy clip, BI-RADS 6.
Grouped round calcifications in the right breast upper outer quadrant, probably benign, BI-RADS 3.

gt_findings.text: Extremely dense breasts (ACR breast density d).

Biopsy-proven malignancy in the left breast at 1 o'clock, upper outer quadrant, 6 cm from the nipple, seen as a 2.2 x 1.8 cm irregular mass with spiculated margins containing the biopsy clip, BI-RADS 6.
1.2 cm group of fine pleomorphic calcifications in the left breast at 4 o'clock, lower outer quadrant, 3 cm from the nipple, separate from the index malignancy, BI-RADS 4C.
Right breast negative for malignancy, with no suspicious mass, calcifications or architectural distortion.
No enlarged axillary lymph nodes on either side.

matches.reasoning: Same biopsy-proven left breast malignancy, sized differently.
Both deny enlarged axillary lymph nodes.
